title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 146 (Co-sureties liable to contribute equally)

content.overview: Section 146 provides that where two or more persons are co-sureties for the same debt or duty, either jointly or severally, and whether under the same or different contracts, and whether with or without the knowledge of each other, the co-sureties, in the absence of any contract to the contrary, are liable, as between themselves, to pay each an equal share of the whole debt, or of that part of it which remains unpaid by the principal debtor.
content.glance: Co-sureties are liable as between themselves to contribute equally, absent a contract to the contrary.
content.study: Where two or more persons are co-sureties for the same debt or duty, either jointly or severally, and whether under the same or different contracts, and whether with or without the knowledge of each other, the co-sureties, in the absence of any contract to the contrary, are liable, as between themselves, to pay each an equal share of the whole debt, or of that part of it which remains unpaid by the principal debtor. Current-law framing: equal contribution is the default; a contrary contract controls.

examples.title: Equal contribution
examples.body: Two co-sureties for the same debt, no contrary contract. They contribute equally as between themselves to the unpaid balance.

hypotheticals.question: Two co-sureties, no agreement as to shares. Principal debtor pays nothing. How do they contribute inter se?
hypotheticals.analysis: Under Section 146, in the absence of a contract to the contrary, each pays an equal share of the unpaid debt.

enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 146 provides for equal contribution as between co-sureties in the absence of a contract to the contrary, whether they are jointly or severally bound, under the same or different contracts, and whether they know of each other or not.
examples: Two co-sureties contribute equally to the unpaid balance.
distinctions: Section 146 is equal contribution; Section 147 addresses contribution where bound in different sums.
